title: compile-time struct size assertions in wire.h catch ABI drift at build time
description: The wc_static_assert2() block at the end of crypto2dev_wire.h checks exact byte sizes for every wire struct. This catches struct layout drift (field reordering, type width changes, missing padding) before it becomes a silent ioctl mismatch (which would produce ENOTTY with no other diagnostic). The expected sizes are hardcoded and must match the kernel uapi. This is the correct approach for a binary ABI boundary: the _IOW/_IOR macros encode struct size into the ioctl command word, so any size mismatch produces a hard failure at the kernel boundary, and the compile-time assert catches it before reaching the kernel. A future contributor might remove the asserts as 'redundant' because the ioctl will fail at runtime anyway — wrong, because runtime ENOTTY has no diagnostic pointing to the struct field that changed.
